title: Double-Booked Driver
description: SwiftCargo deliberately allows a dispatcher to overbook a driver rather than blocking the write — it's the conflicts endpoint's job to surface the mistake, not the write path's job to prevent it. Prove both halves of that design hold.
successCondition: Book two shipments. Assign both to the same driverId (different vehicleId is fine) with overlapping scheduledStart/scheduledEnd windows via two separate PUT /api/fleet/assignments/:shipmentId calls — both calls succeed with 200, proving the write is not blocked. Then GET /api/fleet/conflicts returns a conflicts array containing an entry with resourceType "driver", resourceId equal to the shared driverId, and assignmentIds containing both assignments' ids.
hints: docs/api/fleet.md is explicit that overlapping schedules are never rejected at write time — if your PUT calls fail, you've mixed this up with a different validation case.

"Overlapping" per the conflict logic means scheduledStart of one is before scheduledEnd of the other, and vice versa — make the two windows clearly overlap (e.g. identical windows) to avoid an off-by-a-second edge case.
